description: An open call from a funder (government agency, foundation, or other organization) inviting eligible applicants to submit proposals for grants, contracts, or other financial support; closed or awarded programs are excluded.
examples: NSF CAREER: Faculty Early Career Development Program

fields.name: title
fields.description: The official name of the funding opportunity, usually displayed as a large heading at the top of the page

fields.name: funder
fields.description: The organization or agency issuing the funding, often shown as a logo or label near the title

fields.name: opportunity_id
fields.description: The unique identifier or announcement number assigned by the funder, e.g. CFDA, PAR, RFA, or Horizon topic code

fields.name: description
fields.description: A multi-paragraph summary of the program's goals and what it funds, usually in the main body of the page
fields.example: Funds innovative community-based projects that build resilience to climate-related hazards in coastal and riverine regions.

fields.name: deadline
fields.description: The final date by which full applications must be submitted, typically shown in a sidebar or 'Key Dates' section

fields.name: posted_date
fields.description: The date the opportunity was first published or opened for applications

fields.name: award_amount
fields.description: The maximum or typical funding amount per award, often displayed as a range with a currency symbol (USD, EUR, etc.)

fields.name: eligibility
fields.description: The types of applicants (e.g. universities, nonprofits, individuals) and any geographic restrictions, usually under an 'Eligibility' heading
fields.example: Eligible applicants include U.S.-based nonprofit organizations and accredited public universities.

fields.name: program_url
fields.description: The official URL to the funder's application portal or full announcement page
